verdict.rationale: Penpot documents self-hosting in a private cloud, on-premise, or any controlled environment, using docker compose, an official Helm Chart, OpenShift, or Rancher. The full platform source (frontend, backend, exporter) is public under MPL-2.0, and community users confirm running self-hosted instances. Some hands-on reports describe crashes and lag on self-hosted deployments, but these concern stability, not whether self-hosting is possible. missing for 10: consistent independent evidence of stable self-hosted operation under multi-user load.

support.subject: As a developer, I can self-host the full design platform on my own infrastructure under an open-source license

citations.quote: Penpot is the only open-source design platform that is truly deployment agnostic. Run it in your private cloud, on-premise, or any environment you control.
Use Kubernetes in its different flavors: Deploy the official Helm Chart, Deploy in Openshift, Deploy in Rancher
The full platform source (frontend, backend, exporter) is public in the same repository.
Have been self-hosting this on Docker/Portainer for several weeks for a few people. Works fine so far.
